doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Downbeat Club and meeting Serge Chaloff
summary: Underage, he gets into Philadelphia's Downbeat Club with Serge Chaloff and hears local musicians such as Specs Wright and Jimmy Heath.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So I noticed also, I mean there’s a little bit of research I’ve done here, a lot of research I’ve done here... Behind the Earl Theater was the Downbeat Club.
Right, right. Have you been reading my notes from my book?
Well, you know I’ve been... the combination of that and a lot of other resources there, you know.

And so that to me is a very... it kind of reminded me a little bit of the Howard Theater. On the off nights of course you also... most Monday nights you’d have the Lincoln Colonnades and all those bands would go over there and play for dances. Well, this wasn’t dances, but seems like they also had somewhat of a symbiotic relationship where a lot of these bands or musicians would play there.
Yeah, they’d come there. I happened to meet Serge Chaloff...

... who was a complete nut. And he took me up there, I was underage but he took me up there. They had Specs Wright on drums, Jimmy Golden, pianist, and Jimmy Oliver, tenor saxophonist. Of course Jimmy Heath was up there a lot, and all kinds of great musicians. Red Rodney, so I met a lot of those people when I was a kid. But I
actually, even though I saw Jimmy Heath, I didn’t meet him until Chicago.
But let’s not jump ahead yet on that.
So in the Downbeat Club were you able to gain access to the club or?
Well only if one of the musicians took me up, and sat me in a corner without a drink.
So it definitely wasn’t... a lot of the clubs of course weren’t kid friendly.
No, I couldn’t make the other clubs.
Yeah, they were more kind friendly there.
